Design a detailed implementation plan. Research-only: read files as needed, do not write or modify anything.

## Goal
Transform `/home/node/work/normal_work/cpp_games/cpp_game_with_llm_npcs` (currently a single-NPC chat-window demo) into a **first-person 3D city game**: player walks city streets (WASD + mouse-look), meets **10 LLM-powered NPCs** (shop owners, pedestrians, cops, etc.), presses **'t'** near one to open a dialogue overlay and chat (Ollama backend), **Esc/menu** with **mouse-clickable key-rebinding screen**. Plus: unit tests, a `run.bat` Windows launcher, player documentation, developer README. Priority order from the user: characters & communication first, then world polish.

## Existing code you MUST read and reuse
In `/home/node/work/normal_work/cpp_games/cpp_game_with_llm_npcs`:
- `src/LlmClient.hpp/.cpp` — async Ollama client: background worker thread, request/reply queues, `submit()` returns id, `drainReplies()` non-blocking. POSTs to `/api/chat` with `stream:false`. KEEP this architecture; plan an upgrade to **streaming** (`stream:true`, newline-delimited JSON chunks, partial text pushed to a thread-safe queue so words appear as generated) plus `keep_alive` and a startup warm-up request so the model stays loaded (latency requirements).
- `src/Persona.hpp` — struct {name, role, traits, speakingStyle, knowledgeBoundary, extraDirectives} + renderSystemPrompt(). Reuse for the 10 characters; personas should be data-driven (files under `personas/`), hot-loaded at startup.
- `src/Npc.hpp/.cpp` — persona + bounded history (10 turns), ask/onReplyArrived. Extend with world position.
- `src/DialogUI.hpp/.cpp` — SFML 2D transcript + input box. Reuse as 2D overlay over the 3D scene; needs a streaming-append mode.
- `external/httplib.h`, `external/json.hpp` — vendored single-header HTTP + JSON. Follow this vendoring convention for the test framework (recommend doctest single header in `external/`).
- `config/llm.cfg` — key=value config (host, port, model qwen2.5:3b-instruct, temperature, timeout). Keep; default model stays qwen2.5:3b-instruct.
- `run.sh`, `run.ps1` — launchers that check Ollama reachability then cmake build + run. A `run.bat` must be added (user runs the game on Windows via MSYS2 ucrt64, MinGW Makefiles — see sibling run.ps1).
- `CMakeLists.txt` — CMake 3.20, C++17, SFML 2.6 (graphics/window/system) + Threads.

In `/home/node/work/normal_work/cpp_games/cpp_shooter_game/src/main.cpp` (1159 lines, monolithic) — the 3D reference. Read it carefully and identify exactly which functions/sections to copy/adapt:
- first-person camera + mouse-look with `window.hasFocus()` recentering (~lines 533-544), dt clamping `std::min(0.03f, frameClock.restart().asSeconds())` (~line 1093)
- WASD movement via `sf::Keyboard::isKeyPressed`
- OpenGL rendering: drawTexturedQuad/Box/Cylinder (~lines 186-264), procedural textures, perspective setup
- how it mixes OpenGL 3D with SFML 2D overlay (window.pushGLStates/popGLStates or similar — verify what it actually does for HUD text)
Also `/home/node/work/normal_work/cpp_games/cpp_racing_game/src/main.cpp` has Vec3 math (~lines 348-377).

## Hard constraints
1. **Dev container is headless Linux** (no display; SFML/OpenGL may not even be installed; cmake availability uncertain — g++/make/git/curl confirmed). Therefore architect a strict split:
   - `src/core/` — SFML-free, OpenGL-free game logic: city layout (buildings/streets as data, axis-aligned collision), NPC registry + world positions, proximity query ("nearest NPC within talk radius"), KeyBindings (action→key as portable ints/strings, load/save config file, conflict detection), persona loading, dialogue session state machine (Roaming→Talking→WaitingReply→Streaming), LlmClient + streaming chunk parser. ALL unit tests target core only and must build+run with plain g++ (or cmake if present) with no graphics libs.
   - `src/app/` — SFML+OpenGL: renderer, input mapping, menus, main loop. Compiles on Windows; optionally in container if SFML present.
   - CMake: `core` static lib + `game` exe + `tests` exe; tests must also be buildable by a fallback plain-make path if cmake is missing in the container. Decide and specify the cleanest way.
2. **Tests**: doctest (vendored header) + ctest. LLM protocol tests run against an **in-process fake Ollama** (httplib::Server serving canned /api/chat responses incl. streaming chunks and error cases). Cover: collision, proximity, keybinding save/load/conflicts, persona prompt rendering, history trimming, streaming reassembly, request body shape.
3. **Small commits**: user wants ~2-3 files per commit, each pushed to existing branch `initial_npcs_and_world` (remote https://github.com/bjl14710/cpp_game_with_llm_npcs.git). Commit format `type(scope): description`. Sequence the plan as an ordered commit list, characters/communication first, world second, menu third, docs throughout.
4. **Ollama in container**: plan a rootless install (download Linux binary tarball to ~/.local, `ollama serve` in background) + pull a model for end-to-end testing (qwen2.5:3b-instruct if disk allows; fall back to qwen2.5:1.5b-instruct or llama3.2:1b — check `df -h` first). Game default config stays 3b.
5. **10 characters**: propose the roster (e.g., bakery owner, police officer, taxi driver, barista, librarian, street musician, hot-dog vendor, hardware store owner, tourist, retired teacher) each with distinct persona file and a building/spot on the map.
6. CLAUDE.md rules apply: every public function documented, no TODOs, tests for new logic, don't refactor unrelated code.

## Deliverables in your plan
1. File-by-file architecture (new files, moved files, modified files) with rationale — keep moves minimal to honor small commits.
2. The streaming LlmClient design (thread-safety, partial-reply delivery to main loop, error paths) in enough detail to implement directly.
3. The 3D city scene design: what geometry (street grid, building boxes with name signs, NPC billboards/cylinders), reusing which shooter-game functions.
4. Dialogue interaction flow (proximity hint "Press T to talk", opening/closing overlay, input capture switching between movement and typing).
5. Menu + key rebinding design (mouse hit-testing, persistence file format).
6. Ordered commit sequence (~12-20 commits, ≤3 files each ideally) with files touched per commit and which tests gate each.
7. Verification strategy per phase (what I run in the container after each commit; what only the user can verify on Windows — call those out explicitly).
8. Docs plan: README.md (player), docs/DEVELOPER.md, controls reference.
9. Risks/unknowns (SFML in container, disk for ollama, cmake missing) each with a concrete fallback.

Return the complete plan in markdown. Be specific with file paths and function names so it can be executed without re-research.

1	# cpp_game_with_llm_npcs
2	
3	Milestone 1 of a small game where NPCs hold conversations powered by a single
4	local LLM. This first slice is just a chat window with one companion NPC named
5	**Wren**. No world, no movement, no combat — just dialogue. Later NPCs reuse
6	the same `LlmClient` by design.
7	
8	## Architecture at a glance
9	
10	- **One `LlmClient`** owns the only thread that talks to the LLM. Every NPC
11	  submits requests to it and gets replies back through a thread-safe queue
12	  drained on the main thread.
13	- **`Npc`** holds a `Persona` and a bounded conversation history. The history
14	  is capped at 10 round-trip turns so token usage stays predictable.
15	- **`Persona`** is a small struct rendered into a system prompt. "Jim the
16	  pharmacist" and "Jane the random pedestrian #47" are two `Persona` instances,
17	  not two classes.
18	- **Ollama** runs as a sidecar HTTP service. The C++ side just POSTs JSON to
19	  `localhost:11434/api/chat`. Vendored header-only deps (`cpp-httplib`,
20	  `nlohmann/json`) live in `external/`.
21	
22	## One-time setup
23	
24	### 1. Install Ollama
25	
26	- **Linux:** `curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh`
27	- **Windows:** installer from <https://ollama.com>
28	
29	### 2. Pull a model
30	
31	```
32	ollama pull qwen2.5:3b-instruct
33	```
34	
35	About 2 GB. Runs comfortably on any 6 GB+ NVIDIA GPU. Swap to a different tag
36	later by editing `config/llm.cfg` — no rebuild needed. Suggested alternates:
37	
38	- `llama3.2:3b-instruct` — comparable size, different voice.
39	- `hermes3:8b` — bigger, much better roleplay; needs ~5 GB VRAM at Q4_K_M.
40	
41	### 3. Install SFML 2.6
42	
43	- **Linux (Debian/Ubuntu):** `sudo apt install libsfml-dev`
44	- **Linux (Arch):** `sudo pacman -S sfml`
45	- **Windows:** MSYS2 UCRT64 — `pacman -S mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-sfml`
46	
47	## Build & run
48	
49	Make sure `ollama serve` is running, then:
50	
51	```
52	./run.sh         # Linux / macOS
53	./run.ps1        # Windows (PowerShell, MSYS2 UCRT64)
54	```
55	
56	Either script verifies Ollama is reachable, configures CMake, builds, and
57	launches the game.
58	
59	Or manually:
60	
61	```
62	cmake -S . -B build
63	cmake --build build -j
64	./build/cpp_game_with_llm_npcs
65	```
66	
67	## Talking to Wren
68	
69	Type a line, press Enter. The input box dims while Wren is thinking; it
70	re-enables once the reply lands. Press Esc (or close the window) to quit.
71	
72	## Where to look next
73	
74	- `src/Persona.hpp` — add traits, change voice, or define new NPCs.
75	- `personas/companion.txt` — extra system-prompt directives, hot-reloaded on
76	  every launch (no rebuild).
77	- `config/llm.cfg` — host, port, model tag, temperature.
78	
79	## Future milestones
80	
81	- Multiple NPCs in one scene (architecture already supports it).
82	- Streaming token-by-token replies for a snappier feel.
83	- Persistent per-NPC memory across sessions.
84	- Embed `llama.cpp` directly to drop the Ollama dependency.
85

Research complete. Here is the implementation plan.

---

# Implementation Plan: First-Person 3D City Game with 10 LLM NPCs

## Verified environment facts (no re-research needed)

- **Container**: `g++` and `make` present; **cmake and ctest are NOT installed** (`/usr/bin`, `/usr/local/bin` checked); **no SFML, no GL headers** (`/usr/include/SFML`, `/usr/include/GL` absent). 823 GB disk free — **qwen2.5:3b-instruct (~2 GB) fits easily**, fallback models unnecessary but kept as contingency. 10 cores.
- **Repo**: `/home/node/work/normal_work/cpp_games/cpp_game_with_llm_npcs` is its own git repo, currently on branch `initial_npcs_and_world` tracking `origin` (`https://github.com/bjl14710/cpp_game_with_llm_npcs.git`).
- **httplib is v0.15.3**. Critical finding: there is **no `Post(path, body, content_type, ContentReceiver)` overload**. Client-side streaming must use `httplib::Request` populated manually (`method="POST"`, `path`, `body`, `content_receiver` of type `ContentReceiverWithProgress` = `bool(const char* data, size_t len, uint64_t offset, uint64_t total)`) passed to `Client::send(const Request&)` (declared at `external/httplib.h:1242`). Server side: `Response::set_chunked_content_provider` exists (line 613/5418) for the fake-Ollama streaming tests.
- **Shooter reference** (`/home/node/work/normal_work/cpp_games/cpp_shooter_game/src/main.cpp`):
  - Vec3 math + helpers: lines 36-66; `forwardFromAngles`/`flatForward`/`flatRight`: 345-359.
  - Procedural textures `createTexture`/`makeCheckerTexture`/`makeStripeTexture`/`buildTextures`: 95-152.
  - `setupPerspective` (glFrustum) 158-162, `setupLookAt` (manual matrix) 164-175, `drawTexturedQuad/Box/Cylinder` 186-264, `initOpenGlState` 361-386 (depth, light0, color material, blend).
  - Mouse-look with recenter-when-focused: `handleMouseLook` 533-544. dt clamp `std::min(0.03f, frameClock.restart().asSeconds())` at line 1093. WASD via `sf::Keyboard::isKeyPressed` 517-526.
  - **Gotcha**: `renderHud` (915-1012) demonstrates the correct `window.pushGLStates()/popGLStates()` SFML-over-GL pattern, **but it is dead code — never called**. Only `drawCrosshair` (raw-GL ortho, 883-913) runs. Our overlay must be wired: 3D GL pass → `pushGLStates()` → SFML 2D (nameplates/hint/dialogue/menu) → `popGLStates()` → `window.display()`. Camera there is third-person (eye pulled back 15 units at line 1027); we change to true first-person.
  - GL context setup in `main()` 1053-1075: `sf::ContextSettings` depth 24, GL 2.1, `setMouseCursorVisible(false)`, `setActive(true)`, focus lost/gained handling 1084-1090.
  - Shooter CMake links `OpenGL::GL` via `find_package(OpenGL REQUIRED)` — copy this.

---

## 1. File-by-file architecture

### `src/core/` — SFML-free, GL-free (compiles with plain g++ + pthread; deps only `external/httplib.h`, `external/json.hpp`, std)

| File | Status | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `src/core/LlmClient.hpp/.cpp` | **moved** from `src/`, then extended | Existing worker-thread architecture kept verbatim. Added: streaming (below), `keep_alive`, `warmUp()`. |
| `src/core/Persona.hpp` | **moved** from `src/` | Unchanged struct + `renderSystemPrompt()`. |
| `src/core/Npc.hpp/.cpp` | **moved** from `src/`, extended | Add `Vec3 pos`, `float facingDeg`, `std::string spotId` members + accessors. `ask`/`onReplyArrived`/`trimHistory` untouched. |
| `src/core/Math.hpp` | new (header-only) | `Vec3` + operators, `dot/cross/length/normalize/clampf/degToRad/radToDeg`, adapted from shooter 36-66 (uses no SFML — replace `sf::Color` usages with nothing; colors live in app). |
| `src/core/StreamAssembler.hpp` | new (header-only) | Newline-delimited chunk reassembly + `parseOllamaChunk()` (below). |
| `src/core/Config.hpp/.cpp` | new | `trim()`, `readKv(path)`, `loadLlmConfig(dir)` extracted from current `src/main.cpp:22-67` (logic unchanged, now testable). |
| `src/core/PersonaLoader.hpp/.cpp` | new | Parses `personas/*.persona` files (format below) → `struct LoadedPersona { Persona persona; Vec3 pos; float facingDeg; std::string spotId; }`. `std::vector<LoadedPersona> loadAllPersonas(dir)`. |

Axis-separated collision resolve (try X, then Z), clamp to world bounds. |
| `src/core/World.hpp/.cpp` | new | Free function `int nearestIndexWithin(const std::vector<Vec3>& positions, const Vec3& p, float radius)` (returns -1 if none) + `class World` owning `City` + `std::vector<Npc>`, `Npc* nearestNpcWithin(const Vec3&, float)`. |
| `src/core/KeyBindings.hpp/.cpp` | new | Action enum + portable string key names, load/save, conflict-swap (below). |
| `src/core/DialogueSession.hpp/.cpp` | new | State machine `Roaming → Talking → WaitingReply → Streaming → Talking` (below). |

### `src/app/` — SFML + OpenGL (compiles only on Windows/MSYS2; skipped in container)

| `src/app/Renderer3D.hpp/.cpp` | new (adapted shooter 95-264, 361-386, 778-811, 824-844, 1013-1050) | Textures, `initOpenGlState`, `drawCity`, `drawNpcFigure`, first-person `renderScene`, `worldToScreen` projection for nameplates. |
| `src/app/DialogUI.hpp/.cpp` | **moved** from `src/`, extended | Add streaming line: `beginStreaming(speaker)`, `setStreamingText(text)`, `endStreaming()`, `swallowNextTextEntered()`. |
| `src/app/InputMap.hpp/.cpp` | new | `sf::Keyboard::Key keyFromName(const std::string&)` / `std::string nameFromKey(sf::Keyboard::Key)` lookup tables (letters, digits, arrows, Space, LShift, Escape, Tab, etc.). |

### Other

| `tests/Makefile` | plain-make fallback — **the primary container path since cmake is absent** |

Move policy to keep commits small: `target_include_directories` gains `src/core` (and later `src/app`) so `#include "LlmClient.hpp"` style includes keep working — move commits are then pure `git mv` + one CMake line.

---

## 2. Streaming LlmClient design (implement directly)

### Config and types (`src/core/LlmClient.hpp`)

```cpp
struct LlmConfig {
    // existing fields unchanged...
    std::string keepAlive = "10m";   // sent as "keep_alive" on every request
};

// Partial assistant text, delivered in order per request id.
struct ChatDelta { std::uint64_t id = 0; std::string text; };

class LlmClient {
    // existing API unchanged, plus:
    std::vector<ChatDelta> drainDeltas();   // non-blocking, like drainReplies()
    void warmUp();                          // enqueue internal model-load request
private:
    std::vector<ChatDelta> deltas_;         // guarded by replyMutex_ (renamed outMutex_)
};
// ChatRequest gains: bool internal = false;  (warm-up replies are not enqueued)
```

`config/llm.cfg` gains `keep_alive = 10m` (parsed in `loadLlmConfig`).

### `StreamAssembler.hpp` (core, fully unit-testable, no network)

```cpp
// Reassembles newline-delimited JSON from arbitrary byte slices.
class StreamAssembler {
public:
    // Appends bytes; calls onLine(line) for every complete '\n'-terminated line.
    void feed(std::string_view bytes, const std::function<void(const std::string&)>& onLine);
    // Returns any trailing partial line (end-of-stream flush).
    std::string takeRemainder();
private:
    std::string buffer_;
};

struct OllamaChunk { std::string delta; bool done = false; std::string error; };
// Parses one NDJSON line from /api/chat. Tolerates missing fields; sets error
// for {"error": ...} lines or unparseable JSON.
OllamaChunk parseOllamaChunk(const std::string& line);
```

### `processOne` rewrite (worker thread only — no new threading)

1. Build body exactly as now (`LlmClient.cpp:77-91`) but `{"stream", true}` and `{"keep_alive", config_.keepAlive}`. Warm-up request body: `{"model", model}, {"messages", json::array()}, {"keep_alive", keepAlive}` (Ollama loads the model and returns immediately).
2. Because httplib 0.15.3 lacks a streaming Post overload:
```cpp
httplib::Client cli(config_.host, config_.port);
// timeouts as today (LlmClient.cpp:95-97)
httplib::Request hreq;
hreq.method = "POST";
hreq.path = "/api/chat";
hreq.body = bodyStr;
hreq.set_header("Content-Type", "application/json");
int status = 0;
hreq.response_handler = [&](const httplib::Response& r) { status = r.status; return true; };
StreamAssembler assembler;
std::string full, errorBody;
bool done = false, streamError = false;
hreq.content_receiver = [&](const char* data, size_t len, uint64_t, uint64_t) {
    if (status != 200) { errorBody.append(data, len); return true; }  // collect error JSON
    assembler.feed({data, len}, [&](const std::string& line) {
        OllamaChunk c = parseOllamaChunk(line);
        if (!c.error.empty()) { streamError = true; /* record c.error */ return; }
        if (!c.delta.empty()) { full += c.delta; pushDelta(req.id, c.delta); }  // lock outMutex_
        if (c.done) done = true;
    });
    return !streamError;  // returning false aborts the transfer
};
auto result = cli.send(hreq);
```
3. Result mapping: `!result` → connection error reply (same message as today, `LlmClient.cpp:100-104`); `status != 200` → error with `errorBody`; `streamError` → that error; `done && status == 200` → `ChatReply{ok=true, content=full}`. A stream that closes without `done:true` → `ok=false, "stream ended unexpectedly"`.
4. `workerLoop`: if `req.internal`, discard the reply instead of enqueueing (warm-up). Everything else identical to today.

### Main-thread contract

- Each frame: `drainDeltas()` first, route by id to the dialogue session (UI appends words as they arrive); then `drainReplies()` finalizes via `Npc::onReplyArrived` (unchanged — history only updated on success, partial streamed text discarded by UI on error). Deltas for a closed/abandoned session are simply dropped (id mismatch), so no lifetime issues.
- `warmUp()` called in `app/main.cpp` right after constructing the client.

---

## 3. 3D city scene design

- **World**: 220×220 plane (`halfSize = 110`), perimeter walls reusing shooter `drawTexturedBox` wall pattern (lines 790-793). Ground = single asphalt-checker quad (shooter 779-788); per-block lighter sidewalk quads drawn at y = 0.02 to avoid z-fighting.
- **Layout** (`City::makeDowntown()`): 3×3 blocks, block pitch 64 (48-unit block + 16-unit street), centered on origin. The 10 named buildings sit on block edges facing streets; ~8 unnamed filler boxes complete blocks. Heights 10-26. Each named building gets a bright sign-board quad (textured, tinted per `facadeKind`) on its street face plus a projected 2D text label.
- **NPC figures**: shooter `drawEnemy` style (824-844) — `drawTexturedCylinder` body (radius 0.5, halfHeight 1.0) + head box + small hat/prop box, per-NPC tint from a fixed palette indexed by roster position, rotated by `facingDeg`. Positioned at persona `position`, y so feet touch ground.
- **Camera (first-person)**: `eye = player.pos + {0, 1.7, 0}`, `target = eye + forwardFromAngles(yawDeg, pitchDeg)`, pitch clamped ±75° (not shooter’s 38). Perspective: `setupPerspective(70.f, aspect, 0.1f, 500.f)`.
- **Nameplates/labels**: `std::optional<sf::Vector2f> Renderer3D::worldToScreen(const Vec3&, const CameraPose&, sf::Vector2u viewport)` — apply the same lookAt basis (shooter 164-175) manually, perspective-divide, cull when view-space z ≥ 0; draw `sf::Text` in the SFML overlay pass for NPCs within 30 units and named buildings within 50.
- **Frame order** in `app/main.cpp`: GL 3D pass (no `window.display()` inside, unlike shooter) → `window.pushGLStates()` → nameplates → proximity hint → dialogue overlay or menu → `window.popGLStates()` → `window.display()`.
- Reuse verbatim: `createTexture`, `makeCheckerTexture`, `makeStripeTexture`, `setupPerspective`, `setupLookAt`, `drawTexturedQuad/Box/Cylinder`, `initOpenGlState`, `handleMouseLook`, dt clamp, focus handling. Movement uses `flatForward`/`flatRight` but final position goes through `city.resolveMovement(from, desired, 0.6f)` instead of `keepInsideArena`.

---

## 4. Dialogue interaction flow

- **Playing mode** (per frame): mouse-look (only `if (window.hasFocus())`), WASD via `KeyBindings` → `InputMap`, collision-resolved movement; `world.nearestNpcWithin(player.pos, 6.f)`; if found, bottom-center hint `Press T to talk to Marge` (key name read from bindings, not hardcoded).
- **Open**: `KeyPressed` matching Talk binding while hint active → `AppMode::Dialogue`, `session.open(npcIndex)`, `window.setMouseCursorVisible(true)`, `ui.swallowNextTextEntered()` — this flag makes `DialogUI::handleEvent` drop exactly one `TextEntered` so the ‘t’ keystroke doesn’t appear in the input box (SFML delivers KeyPressed then TextEntered in the same poll cycle).
- **Chat**: events route to `DialogUI` only. Enter (existing `handleEvent` path, `DialogUI.cpp:85-91`) → if `!npc->waiting()`: append player line, `id = npc->ask(text)`, `session.submitted(id)`, `ui.setThinking(true, name)`, `ui.setInputEnabled(false)`.
- **Streaming**: first matching delta → `session` enters `Streaming`, `ui.beginStreaming(name)`; each delta appends; final reply → `npc->onReplyArrived`, `ui.endStreaming()` (converts streaming line to a normal transcript line, or shows the system error line on failure and discards partial text), input re-enabled.
- **Close**: Esc (always) or Menu-bound key in Dialogue → `session.close()`, back to Playing, hide cursor, recenter mouse. If a reply is still in flight, app keeps a tiny `std::vector<std::pair<uint64_t, size_t>> pendingRoutes` (requestId → npcIndex) so the late reply still lands in that NPC’s history.
- **DialogueSession (core, tested)**: states `Roaming/Talking/WaitingReply/Streaming`; `open/close/submitted(id)/deltaArrived(delta)/replyArrived(ok)`; accumulates `streamingText()`; ignores deltas whose id ≠ pending id; error resets to `Talking` with cleared streaming text.

---

## 5. Menu + key rebinding

- **Esc in Playing** → `AppMode::Menu`, cursor visible. Dimmed full-screen `sf::RectangleShape`, buttons **Resume / Controls / Quit** as outlined rectangles + text; hit-testing on `MouseButtonPressed` with `sf::FloatRect::contains(window.mapPixelToCoords(pixel))`; hover highlight via `MouseMoved`.
- **Controls page**: one row per action — label (`Move forward`) + key chip (`W`). Click chip → listening state (chip shows `press a key…`); next `KeyPressed`: `nameFromKey()`; unknown key → ignored. **Conflict policy = swap**: `KeyBindings::rebind(action, keyName)` returns the previously-bound action (if any), which silently receives the rebinding action’s old key; UI shows a 2-second toast `Swapped with Strafe left`. Buttons: `Reset defaults`, `Back`. Every successful change immediately `save()`s.
- **Core `KeyBindings`**: `enum class Action { MoveForward, MoveBackward, StrafeLeft, StrafeRight, Talk, OpenMenu, Count }`; keys stored as portable strings; `defaults()` = W/S/A/D/T/Escape; `actionName(Action)` returns file keys (`move_forward` …) doubling as stable identifiers; `load(path)` (missing/unknown keys keep defaults, reuses `core/Config.hpp` `readKv`), `save(path)`.
- **Persistence** `config/keybindings.cfg`:
  ```
  move_forward = W
  move_backward = S
  strafe_left = A
  strafe_right = D
  talk = T
  menu = Escape
  ```
- Esc always closes menu/dialogue even if `menu` is rebound (documented escape hatch).

### Persona file format (`personas/baker.persona` etc.)

```
name = Marge Holloway
role = bakery owner
traits = warm, gossipy, fiercely proud of her sourdough
style = 1-3 short sentences, motherly, drops baking metaphors
knowledge = Knows the neighborhood, her regulars, bread. Nothing of computers or world news.
spot = bakery
position = -40, 28
facing = 180
---
Freeform extra directives (everything after the --- line goes to extraDirectives verbatim,
```

## 7. Verification strategy per phase

**Container, after every core commit (1-15)**: `make -C tests test` (cmake is absent — this is the primary path; ~10s on 10 cores). Fake-Ollama tests bind `httplib::Server` to port 0/`bind_to_any_port` — fully offline.

**Container, once after commit 9 (end-to-end LLM)**:
1. `df -h /home/node` (already verified: 823 GB free — 3b model fits).
2. Rootless install: `mkdir -p ~/.local/ollama && curl -L https://ollama.com/download/ollama-linux-amd64.tgz | tar -xz -C ~/.local/ollama`, then `~/.local/ollama/bin/ollama serve &` (models default to `~/.ollama`).
3. `~/.local/ollama/bin/ollama pull qwen2.5:3b-instruct`. Fallback chain if pull fails for space/network: `qwen2.5:1.5b-instruct` → `llama3.2:1b` (game config stays `qwen2.5:3b-instruct`; tests read `OLLAMA_TEST_MODEL`).
4. Live tests guarded by env: doctest cases under `TEST_SUITE("live")` with `doctest::skip(std::getenv("OLLAMA_LIVE") == nullptr)`-style gating; run `OLLAMA_LIVE=1 ./tests/run_tests -ts=live` — verifies real streaming deltas arrive incrementally and warm-up keeps latency of second request low.

**Windows-only (user verifies — call out explicitly when delivering commits 16-20)**:
- 16/17: city renders, mouse-look smooth, collision slides along walls, hint appears within ~6 units of an NPC.
- 18: T opens overlay (no stray ‘t’ in input), words stream in, Esc returns to walking, error message when Ollama stopped mid-game.
- 19: Esc menu, clicking chips rebinds, conflict swap toast, `config/keybindings.cfg` updated, bindings survive restart.
- 20: `run.bat` from Explorer and cmd.exe.
Nothing in `src/app/` can be executed in the container; only `g++ -fsyntax-only` sanity is impossible too (no SFML headers) — rely on core/app boundary discipline and user smoke tests.

## 9. Risks and fallbacks

| Risk | Status | Fallback |
|---|---|---|
| SFML/GL absent in container | **Confirmed absent** | Already designed around it: app code never built in container; all logic in core; user does visual verification on Windows. |
| cmake missing in container | **Confirmed missing** | `tests/Makefile` is the primary container build; CMake path maintained for Windows/CI and verified by user. |
| Disk for Ollama | **Cleared — 823 GB free** | Fallback chain 1.5b/1b retained in plan but likely unneeded. |
| httplib streaming-POST overload missing | **Confirmed (0.15.3)** | Use `Request` + `content_receiver` + `Client::send` (verified present at httplib.h:1242, 556). If a hidden incompatibility appears, fallback: upgrade vendored httplib to 0.16+ in a dedicated `build(deps)` commit. |
| ‘t’ leaking into input box on dialogue open | Known SFML behavior | `swallowNextTextEntered()` flag in DialogUI (deterministic, testable by code review). |
| Streamed deltas after dialogue closed / NPC switch | Handled | id-routing: deltas with non-pending ids dropped; `pendingRoutes` map preserves history updates. |
| Model latency on first message | Handled | `warmUp()` empty-messages request at startup + `keep_alive=10m` on every request. |
| Sign text in 3D too complex for legacy GL | Avoided by design | Colored 3D sign boards + projected 2D SFML labels via `worldToScreen`. |
| Mid-sequence broken builds from file moves | Mitigated | Include dirs cover `src/core` so moves don’t touch `#include` lines; every commit leaves `make -C tests test` green. |
